**Section 1.3 --- Exempted Transfers.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following Transfers shall be exempt from the provisions of this Article 1 and Article 2 (each, an \"Exempted Transfer\"), provided that the transferee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement:

\(a\) any Transfer to the spouse, domestic partner, parent, sibling, child, or grandchild of the transferring Key Holder (each, a \"Family Member\"), or to a trust for the benefit of such Family Member or the transferring Key Holder;

\(b\) any Transfer to a revocable living trust of which the transferring Key Holder is the settlor and sole beneficiary during his or her lifetime;

\(c\) any Transfer to an Affiliate of the transferring Key Holder;

\(d\) any Transfer approved in writing by the Board of Directors, including the affirmative vote of at least one director elected by the holders of Series B Preferred Stock;

\(e\) any Transfer in connection with a Deemed Liquidation Event approved in accordance with the Restated Certificate and the Voting Agreement; and

\(f\) any Transfer pursuant to the exercise of a drag-along right under the Voting Agreement.

**Article 2 --- Co-Sale (Tag-Along) Rights**

**Section 2.1 --- Tag-Along Right.** If a Selling Key Holder proposes to Transfer any shares of Transfer Stock and the Company and the Investors have not exercised their respective rights of first refusal with respect to all of the Transfer Stock, each Investor shall have the right to participate in such Transfer (the \"Co-Sale Right\") by selling a number of shares of capital stock of the Company (on an as-converted to Common Stock basis) equal to such Investor\'s pro rata share of the Transfer Stock being transferred by the Selling Key Holder. The Investor\'s \"pro rata share\" for purposes of this Section 2.1 shall be the ratio of (a) the number of shares of Common Stock held by such Investor (on an as-converted, fully-diluted basis) to (b) the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock held by the Selling Key Holder and all Investors (on an as-converted, fully-diluted basis).

Each Investor who wishes to exercise its Co-Sale Right (each, a \"Participating Investor\") shall deliver written notice to the Selling Key Holder within fifteen (15) days after receipt of the Transfer Notice (or, if the rights of first refusal have been exercised only in part, within fifteen (15) days after the Investor ROFR Period). The Participating Investor shall be entitled to sell its shares at the same price per share and on the same terms and conditions as the Selling Key Holder. The Selling Key Holder shall reduce the number of shares of Transfer Stock it sells in such Transfer by the number of shares sold by the Participating Investors.

If a Selling Key Holder consummates a Transfer in violation of this Article 2, each Investor shall have the right to require the Selling Key Holder to purchase from the Investor the number of shares of capital stock that the Investor would have been entitled to sell had the provisions of this Section 2.1 been complied with, at the same price and on the same terms as the Transfer.

**Article 3 --- Miscellaneous**

**3.1 Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to conflicts of law principles.

**3.2 Notices.** All notices hereunder shall be given in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 9.5 of the Purchase Agreement.

**3.3 Amendments.** Any provision of this Agreement may be amended, waived, or modified only upon the written consent of (a) the Company, (b) the holders of a majority of the shares of Preferred Stock then outstanding (on an as-converted basis), and (c) the Key Holders holding a majority of the Transfer Stock then outstanding.

**3.4 Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts.

**3.5 Termination.** This Agreement shall terminate upon the earliest of (a) the consummation of a Qualified IPO, (b) the consummation of a Deemed Liquidation Event pursuant to which the proceeds have been distributed in accordance with the Restated Certificate, or (c) the written agreement of the Company, the holders of a majority of the Preferred Stock (on an as-converted basis), and the Key Holders holding a majority of the Transfer Stock.

**[EXHIBIT E]{.underline}**

**[FOUNDER STOCK RESTRICTION AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**FOUNDER STOCK RESTRICTION AGREEMENT**

This Founder Stock Restriction Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is made and entered into as of February **, 2025, by and between Kaleidoscope Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the \"Company\"), and \_\_\_\_**\_\_ (the \"Founder\").

**RECITALS.** WHEREAS, the Founder holds **\_\_**\_\_ shares of Common Stock, par value \$0.0001 per share, of the Company (the \"Founder Shares\");

WHEREAS, the Company is entering into a Series B Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement dated as of the date hereof (the \"Purchase Agreement\"), with certain investors, pursuant to which such investors are purchasing shares of the Company\'s Series B Preferred Stock;

WHEREAS, as a condition to the closing of the transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement, the Founder and the Company have agreed that the Founder Shares shall be subject to the vesting and repurchase provisions set forth herein;

WHEREAS, this Agreement shall apply to each of Priya Nandakumar (with respect to 4,200,000 Founder Shares) and Marcus Ellingham (with respect to 3,800,000 Founder Shares), each of whom shall execute a separate copy of this Agreement;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises and covenants contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

**Section 1 --- Vesting Schedule**

**Section 1.1 --- Vesting.** (a) The Founder Shares shall be subject to vesting in accordance with the schedule set forth in this Section 1.1. The vesting commencement date shall be the Closing Date (as defined in the Purchase Agreement) (the \"Vesting Commencement Date\"). The total vesting period shall be four (4) years from the Vesting Commencement Date, subject to the prior service credit described in Section 1.1(b) below.

\(b\) **Prior Service Credit.** In recognition of the Founder\'s service to the Company prior to the Vesting Commencement Date, the Founder shall be credited with two (2) years of prior service as of the Vesting Commencement Date. Accordingly, fifty percent (50%) of the Founder Shares shall be deemed fully vested as of the Closing Date and shall not be subject to the Company\'s Repurchase Option (as defined in Section 1.2).

\(c\) **Cliff.** The remaining fifty percent (50%) of the Founder Shares (the \"Unvested Shares\") shall vest as follows: no additional Unvested Shares shall vest during the first twelve (12) months following the Vesting Commencement Date (the \"Cliff Period\"). Upon the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, twenty-five percent (25%) of the total Founder Shares (i.e., one-half of the Unvested Shares) shall vest in a single tranche.

\(d\) **Monthly Vesting.** Following the Cliff Period, the remaining Unvested Shares shall vest in equal monthly installments over the twenty-four (24)-month period commencing on the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date and ending on the fourth anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, such that one hundred percent (100%) of the Founder Shares shall be fully vested on the fourth anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, subject to the Founder\'s continued service with the Company through each applicable vesting date.

\(e\) **Termination of Vesting.** In the event that the Founder\'s employment or other service relationship with the Company terminates for any reason prior to full vesting, vesting shall cease immediately upon such termination, and any Founder Shares that have not vested as of the date of such termination shall remain subject to the Company\'s Repurchase Option.

**Section 1.2 --- Repurchase Option.** (a) In the event that the Founder\'s employment or other service relationship with the Company terminates for any reason (whether voluntary or involuntary, with or without Cause), the Company shall have the option (the \"Repurchase Option\") to repurchase all or any portion of the Unvested Shares held by the Founder as of the date of termination, at a price per share equal to the lower of (i) the original cost per share paid by the Founder for such shares and (ii) the then-current fair market value per share, as determined by the Board of Directors in good faith.

\(b\) The Repurchase Option shall be exercisable by the Company by delivering written notice to the Founder (or the Founder\'s estate or personal representative, as applicable) within ninety (90) days after the date of termination. If the Company does not exercise the Repurchase Option within such period, the Repurchase Option shall lapse with respect to such shares.

**Section 2 --- Acceleration Upon Qualifying Termination Following Change of Control**

**Section 2.1 --- Double-Trigger Acceleration.** In the event of a Change of Control (as defined in the Purchase Agreement), if, within twenty-four (24) months following the closing of such Change of Control, the Founder\'s employment or service with the Company (or its successor or acquiring entity) is terminated (a) by the Company (or its successor or acquiring entity) without Cause, or (b) by the Founder for Good Reason (each, a \"Qualifying Termination\"), then, effective as of the date of such Qualifying Termination, one hundred percent (100%) of the Founder\'s then-unvested Founder Shares shall immediately become fully vested and shall no longer be subject to the Company\'s Repurchase Option.

For purposes of this Agreement:

\(a\) **\"Cause\"** means (i) the Founder\'s willful and continued failure to substantially perform the Founder\'s duties with the Company (other than any such failure resulting from the Founder\'s incapacity due to physical or mental illness), after a written demand for substantial performance is delivered to the Founder specifically identifying the manner in which the Company believes that the Founder has not substantially performed the Founder\'s duties, and the Founder has been given a reasonable opportunity (not less than thirty (30) days) to cure such failure; (ii) the Founder\'s willful engagement in conduct that is demonstrably and materially injurious to the Company, monetarily or otherwise; (iii) the Founder\'s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude; or (iv) the Founder\'s material breach of any written agreement between the Founder and the Company, including any confidentiality, non-competition, or proprietary information agreement, which breach remains uncured for thirty (30) days following written notice.

\(b\) **\"Good Reason\"** means, without the Founder\'s prior written consent, the occurrence of any of the following events: (i) a material diminution in the Founder\'s title, authority, duties, or responsibilities (including a requirement that the Founder report to anyone other than the Board of Directors or the Chief Executive Officer of the surviving or acquiring entity); (ii) a material reduction in the Founder\'s annual base compensation (other than a reduction of not more than ten percent (10%) that is applied proportionally to all similarly situated executives of the Company or its successor); (iii) a relocation of the Founder\'s primary place of employment by more than fifty (50) miles from the Founder\'s then-current primary place of employment; or (iv) any material breach by the Company (or its successor) of this Agreement or any other material agreement between the Founder and the Company. The Founder must provide the Company with written notice of the condition constituting Good Reason within sixty (60) days of its initial occurrence, and the Company shall have thirty (30) days to cure such condition. If the Company fails to cure within such period, the Founder must resign within thirty (30) days following the expiration of the cure period for such resignation to constitute a termination for Good Reason.

**Section 3 --- General Provisions**

**Section 3.1 --- Restrictive Legends.** Each certificate representing the Founder Shares (or book-entry record, as applicable) shall bear the following legends:

\"THE SHARES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE ARE SUBJECT TO A FOUNDER STOCK RESTRICTION AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE HOLDER AND THE COMPANY, A COPY OF WHICH IS ON FILE AT THE PRINCIPAL OFFICE OF THE COMPANY. NO TRANSFER, SALE, ASSIGNMENT, PLEDGE, HYPOTHECATION, OR OTHER DISPOSITION OF THE SHARES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE MAY BE MADE EXCEPT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS OF SUCH AGREEMENT.\"

\"THE SHARES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED, OR UNDER ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS AND MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD, OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED, PLEDGED, OR HYPOTHECATED UNLESS AND UNTIL REGISTERED UNDER SUCH ACT AND APPLICABLE STATE SECURITIES LAWS OR UNLESS THE COMPANY HAS RECEIVED AN OPINION OF COUNSEL OR OTHER EVIDENCE REASONABLY SATISFACTORY TO THE COMPANY THAT SUCH REGISTRATION IS NOT REQUIRED.\"

**Section 3.2 --- Transfer Restrictions.** During the period in which any Founder Shares remain unvested and subject to the Company\'s Repurchase Option, the Founder shall not sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, or otherwise dispose of any Unvested Shares, except (a) as otherwise permitted under the Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement, (b) upon exercise of the Company\'s Repurchase Option, or (c) with the prior written consent of the Board of Directors.

**Section 3.3 --- Section 83(b) Election.** The Founder acknowledges that the Founder has been advised by the Company and the Company\'s counsel to consult with the Founder\'s own tax advisor regarding the availability and advisability of filing an election under Section 83(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), with respect to the Founder Shares. The Founder understands that any such election must be filed with the Internal Revenue Service within thirty (30) days of the date of this Agreement and that the Founder is solely responsible for timely filing such election. The Company shall have no liability or obligation to the Founder for any failure by the Founder to timely file a Section 83(b) election.

**Section 3.4 --- Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to conflicts of law principles.

**Section 3.5 --- Spousal Consent.** If the Founder is married, the Founder\'s spouse shall execute a Spousal Consent in the form attached hereto as Annex I, acknowledging and agreeing to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. The failure of the Founder\'s spouse to execute such consent shall not affect the validity or enforceability of this Agreement.

**Section 3.6 --- Entire Agreement.** This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter.

**Section 3.7 --- Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

**[FORM OF LEGAL OPINION OF WHITFIELD & CRANE LLP]{.underline}**

The legal opinion to be delivered by Whitfield & Crane LLP, counsel to the Company, at the Closing shall address, among other matters: (i) the due organization, valid existence, and good standing of the Company under the laws of the State of Delaware; (ii) the authorization and valid issuance of the Shares; (iii) the absence of conflicts between the Transaction Agreements and the Company\'s organizational documents or material agreements; (iv) the absence of required governmental consents (other than those already obtained); and (v) compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws in connection with the issuance of the Shares.

 "Delete the proviso so the Series B consent to any Deemed Liquidation Event is unconditional, as the term sheet provides."),

 "Medium",
 "Delete the blank-check language or make any new series subject to 60% Series B consent. Consider reducing authorized Preferred to the designated amounts plus a cushion."),

 "Restore a 7-member Board with two Independent Directors and the full independence and experience criteria. Name or pin down the second Series B designee before closing (TS §3.1(a)). Set a timeline and fallback mechanism for appointing the Independent Directors."),

 "Medium",
 "Add NVCA-style charter provisions: the Series B elects two directors, the Series A elects one, the Common elects two, and the rest are elected by all holders voting together, with class-based removal and vacancy filling."),
("G-9","Drag-along approval",
 "TS §3.3: drag triggered only if approved by both (a) a majority of the outstanding Common, voting separately, and (b) at least 60% of the Preferred (as-converted), voting separately; “neither class alone is sufficient.” Obligations: vote for, waive appraisal, take reasonably necessary actions.",
 "Voting Agreement §2.1: triggered by “a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock … voting together as a single class” only. There is no Common approval. Preferred threshold is a majority, not 60%.",
 "The draft lets the Preferred alone drag the Common, and at a lower threshold. Orchard Hill alone holds about 78% of the as-converted Preferred (4.8M Series A + 4.30M Series B of 11.50M), so it could unilaterally drag every stockholder. This is a fundamental governance change.  "Critical",
 "Restore the dual approval: majority of Common and 60% of Preferred, each voting separately. Keep the §2.2 protective conditions. Consider whether the Board should also approve, and whether a Series B-specific consent applies (see G-4)."),
("G-10","Board observers",
 "TS §3.1: any Investor holding ≥ $4,000,000 of Series B (by original purchase price) may designate one non-voting observer to attend all Board meetings and receive all materials, subject to customary exclusions for conflicts of interest and privilege. All three Investors qualify at closing.",
 "Voting Agreement §1.2: same $4M threshold, aggregated for affiliated Investors; adds committee meetings; adds an exclusion for “competitively sensitive information”; observers bound by the confidentiality applicable to directors.",
 "The thresholds match. The added “competitively sensitive information” exclusion is broader than the term sheet and could be used to exclude observers. Aggregation across affiliates is a sensible clarification. Observer rights would sit better in the IRA (the NVCA location), together with the Management Rights Letter.",
 "Low",
 "Delete or narrow the competitive-sensitivity exclusion (for example, limit it to an observer affiliated with an actual competitor). Consider moving observer rights to the IRA. Confirm that Ridgeway, at exactly $4,000,000, qualifies under the final, recomputed share numbers (see E-2)."),
("G-11","Charter amendment protection and Series A protective provision",
 "TS §3.2(a): 60% Series B consent to any adverse charter or bylaw amendment.",
 "Restated Certificate Article VII requires consent of the affected series “in accordance with Section 4.6,” which currently means a majority of the Series B. §4.6(c) gives the Series A a veto only over amendments that are disproportionately adverse to the Series A.",
 "The Article VII cross-reference imports the wrong (majority) threshold. The term sheet is silent on the Series A protective provision. Because Orchard Hill holds all of the Series A, the provision gives it a separate veto, which should be confirmed with the client.",
 "Low",
 "Conform Article VII to 60% of the Series B. Confirm with the client the scope of any Series A class vote (DGCL §242(b)(2) applies in any event)."),
]

(d) Adding wind-up, sinking funds and Series B Director approval of repurchases helps investors, but none of it is in the term sheet.",
 "Medium",
 "Fix the Board cap at seven (7) in the charter. Track the term sheet wording on business change. Extend (ii) to “rights, preferences or privileges” generally, as in TS §3.2(c). The investor-favorable additions can be kept but should be flagged to Company counsel as additions."),
("G-6","“Blank check” preferred and unprotected junior securities",
 "TS §3.2(c) protects against senior and parity securities. The TS does not contemplate Board authority to designate new series.",
 "Restated Certificate §4.1: of 15,000,000 authorized Preferred, 3,504,762 shares are undesignated and “may be issued from time to time in one or more series … as shall be fixed by resolution of the Board.”",
 "This gives the Board blank-check authority over about 3.5M shares of preferred. Junior series, and series with special voting or board rights, could be issued without any Series B vote, and §4.6(b)(ii) does not cover rights other than economics.",
 "Medium",
 "Delete the blank-check language or make any new series subject to 60% Series B consent. Consider reducing authorized Preferred to the designated amounts plus a cushion."),
("G-7","Board composition",
 "TS §3.1: seven (7) directors: 2 Series B Directors (Theodore Hargrove plus one Lead Investor designee), 1 Series A Director (Simone Aldridge), 2 Common Directors (Nandakumar and Ellingham), and two (2) Independent Directors mutually agreed by the Series B Directors and the CEO, who are not employees, officers or affiliates of the Company or any Investor and have relevant industry or operational experience.",
 "Voting Agreement §1.1: six (6) directors with one (1) Independent Director; independence test omits the “relevant industry or operational experience” requirement and adds non-affiliation with Key Holders; the initial Independent Director is designated “prior to or promptly following the Closing.” SPA §7.3 defers to the Voting Agreement.",
 "One independent seat is dropped. That changes the Board balance from 3 investor-designated seats of 7 (with 2 jointly selected) to 3 of 6, and gives the investor and common blocs an even 3–3 split on non-independent seats, which affects the deadlock dynamics. The draft does not satisfy closing condition TS §5.3(e), which requires a Voting Agreement providing for the TS §3.1 Board.",
 "High",
 "Restore a 7-member Board with two Independent Directors and the full independence and experience criteria. Name or pin down the second Series B designee before closing (TS §3.1(a)). Set a timeline and fallback mechanism for appointing the Independent Directors."),
("G-8","Series B and Series A director election rights in the charter",
 "TS §2.5: the Series B, voting as a separate class, “shall be entitled to elect the Series B Directors.”",
 "Restated Certificate Article V leaves the number of directors to the Bylaws and Voting Agreement and contains no class-vote election rights; seats exist only contractually in the Voting Agreement.",
 "The class election right the term sheet calls for is missing from the charter. A purely contractual right is weaker (enforcement against non-signatories, transferees and future holders) and does not support the vacancy and removal mechanics under DGCL §141(k) and §223.",
 "Medium",
 "Add NVCA-style charter provisions: the Series B elects two directors, the Series A elects one, the Common elects two, and the rest are elected by all holders voting together, with class-based removal and vacancy filling."),
("G-9","Drag-along approval",
 "TS §3.3: drag triggered only if approved by both (a) a majority of the outstanding Common, voting separately, and (b) at least 60% of the Preferred (as-converted), voting separately; “neither class alone is sufficient.” Obligations: vote for, waive appraisal, take reasonably necessary actions.",
 "Voting Agreement §2.1: triggered by “a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock … voting together as a single class” only. There is no Common approval. Preferred threshold is a majority, not 60%.",
 "The draft lets the Preferred alone drag the Common, and at a lower threshold. Orchard Hill alone holds about 78% of the as-converted Preferred (4.8M Series A + 4.30M Series B of 11.50M), so it could unilaterally drag every stockholder. This is a fundamental governance change. Founders and Common holders will object, and the clause is open to fiduciary and enforceability challenge. The §2.2 conditions (same consideration, limited reps, pro rata and several indemnity) are useful additions consistent with market practice.",
 "Critical",
 "Restore the dual approval: majority of Common and 60% of Preferred, each voting separately. Keep the §2.2 protective conditions. Consider whether the Board should also approve, and whether a Series B-specific consent applies (see G-4)."),
("G-10","Board observers",
 "TS §3.1: any Investor holding ≥ $4,000,000 of Series B (by original purchase price) may designate one non-voting observer to attend all Board meetings and receive all materials, subject to customary exclusions for conflicts of interest and privilege. All three Investors qualify at closing.",
 "Voting Agreement §1.2: same $4M threshold, aggregated for affiliated Investors; adds committee meetings; adds an exclusion for “competitively sensitive information”; observers bound by the confidentiality applicable to directors.",
 "The thresholds match. The added “competitively sensitive information” exclusion is broader than the term sheet and could be used to exclude observers. Aggregation across affiliates is a sensible clarification. Observer rights would sit better in the IRA (the NVCA location), together with the Management Rights Letter.",
 "Low",
 "Delete or narrow the competitive-sensitivity exclusion (for example, limit it to an observer affiliated with an actual competitor). Consider moving observer rights to the IRA. Confirm that Ridgeway, at exactly $4,000,000, qualifies under the final, recomputed share numbers (see E-2)."),
("G-11","Charter amendment protection and Series A protective provision",
 "TS §3.2(a): 60% Series B consent to any adverse charter or bylaw amendment.",
 "Restated Certificate Article VII requires consent of the affected series “in accordance with Section 4.6,” which currently means a majority of the Series B. §4.6(c) gives the Series A a veto only over amendments that are disproportionately adverse to the Series A.",
 "The Article VII cross-reference imports the wrong (majority) threshold. The term sheet is silent on the Series A protective provision. Because Orchard Hill holds all of the Series A, the provision gives it a separate veto, which should be confirmed with the client.",
 "Low",
 "Conform Article VII to 60% of the Series B. Confirm with the client the scope of any Series A class vote (DGCL §242(b)(2) applies in any event)."),
]
EOF
echo ok'

("R-1","Preemptive right (right of first refusal on new issuances)",
 "TS §4.1: each holder of Preferred has a pro rata right to buy new equity “on the same terms and at the same price as offered to third-party purchasers”; exceptions: Excluded Issuances (TS §2.4), equipment leasing, bank borrowings and similar debt financings; pro rata share on a fully-diluted, as-converted basis; an exercise period of “not less than fifteen (15) business days” from written notice.",
 "IRA §4.1: grants the right and defines pro rata share consistently, but contains no notice, exercise period, same-terms or over-allotment mechanics.  "High",
 "Add full NVCA §4 mechanics: Company notice, at least 15 business days to exercise, same price and terms, over-allotment, a 90-day sale window, and termination at a Qualified IPO or Deemed Liquidation Event. ("R-2","Co-sale (tag-along) and ROFR Agreement",

 "Exhibit D §§1.1–2.1: co-sale and secondary ROFR run only to “Investors,” defined as the Series B investors on Schedule 1. The Company has a first ROFR (15 days), then the Investors (15 days). ("R-3","Demand registration",

 "IRA §2.1: 30% Initiating Holders and two demands, consistent. Adds a waiting period (earlier of the 5th anniversary or 180 days post-IPO) and a minimum offering size above $10,000,000. Omits the 180-day post-registration blackout. A demand counts only once effective for 120 days.",
 "The added waiting period and $10M minimum are market-standard NVCA terms but go beyond the term sheet.  "Medium",
 "Decide with the client whether to accept the NVCA additions. Conform the Registrable Securities definition. Add the 180-day post-registration limit, or confirm it was intentionally dropped."),
("R-4","S-3 / F-3 registration",
 "TS §4.3: unlimited S-3/F-3 registrations; minimum $5,000,000 aggregate offering price per registration; maximum two in any 12-month period.",
 "IRA §2.2: unlimited, maximum two per 12 months, consistent; minimum is $1,000,000.",
 "The $1M minimum is lower than the agreed $5M. This favors investors but deviates from the term sheet.",
 "Low",
 "Conform to $5,000,000 unless the client wants to press for the lower number."),
("R-5","Piggyback registration and cutbacks",

 "IRA §2.3: notice given “promptly,” with no minimum lead time; cutback allocated “pro rata among the Holders requesting inclusion.”",
 "The agreed 20-day notice period is missing. Allocating the cutback only among Holders (rather than “all selling stockholders”) changes the agreed priority, and there is no rule that Holder shares are cut back before or alongside non-Holder sellers.",
 "Medium",

("R-6","Company lock-up vs. holder lock-up",

 "IRA §2.5: imposes a 180-day (plus up to 30-day extension) market-standoff lock-up on the Holders, with commercially reasonable efforts to bind directors, officers and >1% holders. There is no Company lock-up.",
 "The draft inverts the agreed covenant. It omits the protection the term sheet gave investors (a Company holdback) and adds a restriction on investors that the term sheet did not include.  "TS §4.3: the Company pays all registration expenses except underwriting discounts and commissions on the selling holders’ shares.",

 "Low",
 "Accept the selling-holder counsel. Consider whether stock transfer taxes should stay with the Holders."),

 "IRA §1 defines “Major Investor” as ≥ $2,000,000 aggregate Original Issue Price, but Art. 3 never uses it and delivers to “each holder of Preferred Stock (and any holder of Common Stock issued upon conversion).” Quarterly statements cover only the first three fiscal quarters.  "(a) The eligibility threshold is both changed ($2M by price is about 478,263 shares, not 500,000) and not applied, so the rights reach every Preferred holder and converted holder, which the term sheet expressly excludes (“limited to Major Investors”). (b) Fourth-quarter unaudited statements are dropped. (c) The term sheet’s confidentiality obligation has no counterpart; the IRA needs a confidentiality covenant (NVCA §3.4). (d) The Board can accept a qualified audit opinion. (e) The CFO/CEO certification and the narrative description are useful additions. There are no inspection rights, and no termination of information rights at IPO or for competitors; consider both.",
 "Medium",
 "Define Major Investor as ≥ 500,000 Preferred shares (as-converted, adjusted for splits) and limit Art. 3 to Major Investors. Cover all four quarters within 45 days. Add a confidentiality covenant and the customary competitor carve-out. Strike the “other opinion” language, or require Series B Director approval."),
("R-9","Information to be delivered at signing: financial statements rep",
 "TS §4.4(b) assumes audited annual statements by the Company’s independent registered accounting firm, Redwood Alliance Accounting LLP. TS §5.3(a) requires financial diligence satisfactory to the Lead Investor.",
 "SPA §4.9(a): the Company delivers only unaudited annual statements for FY2023 and FY2024 and unaudited quarterlies, even though §4.9(b) names Redwood Alliance as the Company’s “independent auditor.”",
 "No audited financials are represented for a $28M round at a company that has an auditor. Either audits exist and should be delivered and represented, or they do not exist, which is a diligence point.",
 "Medium",
 "Ask whether audited FY2023 (and FY2024, when available) statements exist. If so, require delivery and an audited-statements rep. Otherwise consider a covenant to deliver the FY2024 audit within 120 days, consistent with IRA §3.1(b)."),

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

("F-1","Single-trigger acceleration",
 "TS §5.1: on a Change of Control, 25% of each Founder’s then-unvested shares vest immediately at closing of the Change of Control.",
 "Exhibit E (Founder Stock Restriction Agreement): no single-trigger acceleration. Section 2 provides double-trigger acceleration only.",

 "Exhibit E §2.1: twenty-four (24) months.",
 "The protection window is doubled, in the founders’ favor, which raises the retention cost for an acquirer and could depress deal value.",

# 1. Executive Summary

Company counsel's transmittal email says the draft "reflects the agreed term sheet with standard NVCA model language," with only "a few provisions ... refined to reflect current market practice" and to address "mechanical and administrative matters." That description is not accurate. The draft departs from the executed term sheet on several core economic and governance terms, omits several bargained-for protections, and contains material arithmetic and drafting errors, some of which are carried over from the term sheet itself. Some deviations favor the Investors (for example, participation, a higher expense cap and a lower S-3 threshold). We flag those as well: they depart from the agreed deal, will likely be reversed, and accepting them silently risks a re-trade and delay to the Feb. 28 signing.

**Most significant issues (Critical):**

- **E-1 Price per share / option pool "pre-money" mechanics:** The SPA carries forward a mathematical defect in the term sheet and, in doing so, shifts pool dilution onto the Series B.

- **E-3 Liquidation priority: Series B senior vs. pari passu:** This reverses the agreed seniority.

- **E-4 Participation: non-participating vs. capped participating:** This is a material departure from the agreed structure.

- **E-6 Automatic conversion: Qualified IPO thresholds:** Lowering both thresholds lets the Company force conversion, and so wipe out the Series B preference and protective provisions, in a smaller IPO at a lower price than agreed.

- **G-4 Protective provisions: Deemed Liquidation Event veto:** The proviso largely removes the M&A veto.

- **G-9 Drag-along approval:** The draft lets the Preferred alone drag the Common, and at a lower threshold.

**Other high-priority issues (High):**

- **E-2 Per-investor share allocation and aggregate purchase price**

- **E-5 Dividend priority**

- **G-1 Protective provisions: approval threshold**

- **G-2 Protective provisions: debt incurrence**

- **G-3 Protective provisions: related-party transactions**

- **G-7 Board composition**

- **R-1 Preemptive right (right of first refusal on new issuances)**

- **R-6 Company lock-up vs. holder lock-up**

- **F-2 Double-trigger window**

- **F-3 Vesting schedule mechanics**

- **C-7 Supersession of binding term sheet provisions (exclusivity, confidentiality)**

- **O-4 Capitalization representations and schedules**

*Issue count: 44 substantive items (Critical 6; High 12; Medium 19; Low 7), plus 14 drafting and conforming items in Section 9.*

# 2. Severity Key and Approach

- **Critical:** Changes a core economic or control term of the executed term sheet. Must be fixed before signing.

- **High:** Material deviation or omission of a negotiated term, or an error that affects money or shares. Fix in the first markup.

- **Medium:** Deviation, gap or ambiguity that should be corrected or expressly accepted.

- **Low:** Minor, conforming or investor-favorable point. Confirm the client's position.

Method: we compared each term sheet section (§§1.1--6.5 and App. A) against the SPA and each exhibit, recomputed all share, price and percentage figures, and cross-checked the separately circulated cap table and the transmittal email.
